items.title: This repository is the go-to-market source of truth
items.verdict: The PicoGTMBrain repository holds the governed go-to-market for both audiences. Strategy, claims, status, and voice are changed here first, in the order ledger, master context, decision log, copy. CLAUDE.md wins if the routers disagree.
items.rationale: The GTM build produced dashboards, a walkthrough, and a Google folder. Those are deliverables. This repo is the operating system that keeps them true.
items.does_not_change: any decision below, any price, any target, any channel.
items.downstream: the Google folder documents and the walkthrough are regenerated from this repo's ledgers when a ledger changes. Owner: founder.

items.title: Launch calendar and build list
items.verdict: Week 1 starts Monday 2026-11-09. Build order: inventory webhook (week 1), sync failure email (2), first insight email and weekly summary (4), partner ledger, payout run, and proof capture point (6), monthly usage summary (8), the words against the catalog check (10). The founding cohort opens 2026-12-01, after Cyber Monday. Day 60 review in week 12, day 90 review in week 13.
items.rationale: Each item is the touch-point for one funnel stage, sequenced so sync works before installs and partner tooling before the partner page.
items.does_not_change: prices, the partner terms, the channels.
items.reopen_when: an item slips by more than two weeks. The founder and engineer move the next block's scope.

items.title: Planning bands where trackers are silent
items.verdict: Merchant Level 1: 100 or more products, 10,000 to 100,000 monthly sessions, 1 to 10 people, about $150,000 to $3 million a year. Level 2: 250 or more products, 100,000 to 1 million sessions, 10 to 50 people. 2% of sessions start a conversation (Assumption). Implementer Level 1: 1 to 5 people, under $250,000, 2 to 10 client stores. Level 2: 6 to 50 people, $1 million to $20 million, 10 to 100 client stores (Assumption).
items.rationale: Catalog cutoffs are researched (StoreLeads, 2026: 28.2% of stores sell 100 or more products). Sessions decide the band, because order values differ.
items.does_not_change: any customer copy. Bands never appear in copy.
items.reopen_when: the founding cohort's intake answers and first 30 days of conversations, and the first 30 session applications.

items.title: Legal and platform conduct
items.verdict: A US private mailbox in Pico's name is the postal address on every commercial email from week 1. Cold email goes to US recipients only in the first 90 days, then UK companies and LLPs only, never UK sole traders, never cold to the EU. Sessions found on a platform are paid on that platform, and no partner invitation goes inside Upwork or Fiverr. Counsel reviews the partner terms in week 5. Permission forms and a terms clause are ready in week 2. Invoice-paid implementers sign a session agreement and give a W-9 or W-8BEN.
items.rationale: CAN-SPAM needs a postal address and an opt-out. PECR treats sole traders as individuals. Fiverr bars steering off the platform, and Upwork's term covers payments for 24 months.
items.does_not_change: the fee, the shares, the channel mix.
items.reopen_when: counsel advises otherwise, or either platform changes its terms.

items.title: Listing, reviews, targets, and feedback cadence
items.verdict: The listing is "Pico AI Shopping Assistant" in the Chat category, search terms AI shopping assistant, product finder, product discovery. Screenshots lead with the Shopper Words Test, then cards, then Analytics, then the plan page. Reviews are asked for only after the merchant has opened Analytics and made one fix, replies within 2 business days, no incentives. Merchant and implementer 90-day targets are in innovation/metrics.json. Founding merchants get a monthly 30-minute call, partners a quarterly call and a digest after each batch of 10 sessions.
items.rationale: Merchants compare chat apps first, and the first reviews set the listing's tone.
items.does_not_change: the conversation definition or any price.
items.reopen_when: listing visit to install falls below 2% at day 30, or call attendance falls below half.

items.title: Partner program terms and operations
items.verdict: 25% of each referred store's subscription charges for 24 months, 30% for lead partners at 5 active paying stores, 10% managed share, one share per store, no cash bounty. Payouts monthly on the 15th for charges Shopify paid out the prior month, $50 minimum carried forward, PayPal or bank transfer. Attribution by deal registration on the myshopify domain, merchant-confirmed, valid 90 days. Referral traffic is routed setup requests, never a promised volume. No separate agency price. The partner page goes live in week 6.
items.rationale: Above the 20% floor that Gorgias and Shopify set. A recurring share pays only while the store pays.
items.does_not_change: merchant prices, and Shopify Billing charging each store.
items.reopen_when: 12 months in, partner-referred stores pass 25% of paying stores, 2 attribution disputes in a quarter, or 50 routed requests a month.

items.title: Paid sessions, interviews, and the session cohort
items.verdict: $150 for a fixed scope of up to 90 minutes: sandbox, install on a development or permissioned client store, the Shopper Words Test, timed setup, feedback form. Pico pays platform fees. Optional $75 interview for 30 minutes. 30 sessions in 60 days from week 1: Upwork 15, Fiverr 5, email 6, LinkedIn 4.
items.rationale: About $100 an hour, inside the research incentive range for engineers and above the roughly $100 gig for installing an AI chat app.
items.reopen_when: fewer than 10 qualified applicants per Upwork post (raise to $200), fewer than half accept the interview, or day 30 completion rates by channel.

items.title: The 90-day budget and the runway gate
items.verdict: $9,000 over 90 days, capped at $3,000 a month: sessions $4,984, interviews $1,215, ScoreApp and Sales Navigator $477, sending domain and US mailbox $180, counsel $1,000, held back $1,144. Spend is released in 30-day blocks, each needing 6 months of company runway after it. If a block fails, paid sessions pause and outreach continues on email, LinkedIn, and the scorecard.
items.does_not_change: company burn, which sits outside the plan.
items.reopen_when: each 30-day block, and the day 90 review.

items.title: The founding cohort
items.verdict: 20 US stores, 50% off any paid plan for 6 billing periods through a Shopify Billing subscription discount, a monthly feedback call, a direct line to the founder, roadmap input. A written case study request at day 60. Opens 2026-12-01 and closes at 20 stores or 90 days after the listing goes live.
items.reopen_when: it fills before day 60: open a second cohort of 20.

items.title: Pricing structure
items.verdict: Yearly plans give two months free: Growth $490, Pro $990, Scale $2,990. Scale is $299 a month for 6,000 conversations with an onboarding call, and custom plans above it at about $0.05 a conversation. Model cost ceiling $0.02 a conversation (Assumption), which puts gross margin before other costs at 76% on Growth and 60% on Pro and Scale. Month 6 target mix: Free 60% of active installs, paying stores 70% Growth, 22% Pro, 8% Scale.
items.does_not_change: Free, Growth, and Pro monthly prices.
items.reopen_when: fewer than 10% choose yearly by month 6, 3 stores request a custom plan, measured model cost exceeds the ceiling in the first 30 days of logs, or the month 6 mix review.

items.title: What a conversation is, and what happens at the quota
items.verdict: A conversation is a chat thread with at least one AI reply, counted once per shopper and device per 24 hours, fair use 50 AI replies. At the quota: alerts at 80% and 100%, open conversations finish, paid plans get 10% grace at no charge, then the launcher pauses until the next cycle or an upgrade. No overage charge, ever.
items.rationale: Billing surprise is the category's most frequent complaint class, so a capped quota becomes a positioning line once it ships.
items.reopen_when: 3 support tickets about the definition in a month, or pauses drive more than 20% of uninstall reasons.

items.title: One value metric, development stores, and the workspace trigger
items.verdict: Every feature is on every plan, and plans differ only in conversations a month. Paid plans are free for testing on partners' development stores. The multi-store workspace is built when 10 partners each have 3 or more active paying stores, and until then a partner takes the admin role on each store.
items.reopen_when: a feature needs gating to protect margin, or the workspace trigger fires.

items.title: Product claims: themes, headless, speed, stock, catalog text
items.verdict: Theme claims cover Online Store themes through the theme app embed, tested on Dawn and Horizon before launch. Headless is not claimed. Speed budget 10 Lighthouse points on Dawn, measured in week 1 and published, never "no impact". Stock copy is "Stock as of your last catalog sync" until the inventory webhook ships. No claim that Pico translates catalog text.
items.does_not_change: the install path or the checklist.
items.reopen_when: a theme issue appears in 2 sessions, a Hydrogen store passes a session, the speed test fails the budget, or the webhook ships.

items.title: Launch scope: handoff, orders, channels, integrations
items.verdict: Human handoff is not built or claimed. Order, return, and policy answers are out of scope by design. WhatsApp and Instagram wait for the GCC. The first integration is a GA4 event export, built with revenue attribution after the founding cohort.
items.rationale: Positioning against chat apps rests on not trying to answer everything.
items.reopen_when: 5 of 20 founding stores ask for handoff or order answers, or 2 uninstall reasons cite them in a month, or the GCC opens, or the founding cohort closes.

items.title: Geography: USA first, the GCC on a trigger
items.verdict: Global, USA first. The GCC opens when the US founding cohort is full and at least 5 GCC stores have asked for Pico in one quarter. Until then GCC material is reference only.
items.does_not_change: Arabic right to left as a shipped feature line.
items.reopen_when: the trigger fires: size the GCC and review messaging channels.

items.title: Two standalone go-to-markets, slates stand, Shopware deferred
items.verdict: Merchants and implementers each get a standalone go-to-market. Both competitor slates stand as built. Shopware 6 and custom stores wait for a deferred third run, and EGP prices appear in no merchant or implementer asset.
items.does_not_change: Shopware 6 and the custom catalog API as shipped product.
items.reopen_when: a slate slot fails its page-loaded check, or the third run starts.

items.title: Operating basis and pre-launch state
items.verdict: An Egypt-based team selling in USD worldwide (Researched). Founder-led, two people (Assumption). No channel tried with results, and no installs, stores, payers, or rating recorded (Researched).
items.does_not_change: anything customer-facing. The team basis sizes timeframes only.
items.reopen_when: the team grows, the listing goes live, or the first 30 days of results arrive.

items.title: Open proof, never invented proof
items.verdict: The customer proof log is empty and closed. Every proof slot carries open proof: an invitation to check a claim now, naming what and where. A case study enters only with exact wording, a source, and recorded permission from everyone it names.
items.does_not_change: the narrowed claims, which still govern every line.
items.reopen_when: the first case study has recorded permission: it replaces the open proof line in its drill.

items.title: Website and listing
items.verdict: Website: picofinds.com. The listing is submitted in week 1 as "Pico AI Shopping Assistant", live target week 3, buffer to week 6. Until it is live, every merchant call to action is "Connect your store". The site is aligned with the US-first plan before the first implementer email: Shopify and English first, Shopware on its own page, three broad lines replaced, new headline "An AI shopping assistant for Shopify that answers from your own catalog."
items.does_not_change: implementer sessions, which run on development stores and need no approved listing.
items.reopen_when: the listing is approved: every call to action switches to the listing.

items.title: Approve the six examples in examples/ as voice references
items.verdict: Approve the six examples in examples/ as voice references. Owner: founder. Until approved they are proposed gold standards, five built only from copy-bank lines and the sync failure email written as the brain's live test on 2026-11-05.

items.title: Tone anchors
items.verdict: Tone anchors. Two brands whose voice is right for Pico, two that are wrong. Owner: founder.

items.title: Which AI tools the team runs
items.verdict: Which AI tools the team runs. Doors ship for 19 tools with their own file, for agents that read AGENTS.md such as Zed, Jules, and Amp, for MCP and HTTP clients, and for chat windows, rendered from one source, so a stale door fails CI instead of drifting. Prune the ones nobody uses from RULE_DOORS and COMMAND_TOOLS in tools/brain.py. Owner: founder.

items.verdict: Company runway and burn. Outside the plan, read by the runway gate (D32). Owner: founder as CFO.
